rows.reason: The arrow is reached only if `decodeUnknownCallReview` fails on a record just returned by `readMany`. Both production stores already apply the registered schema validate to every returned record (`in-memory-record-store.ts:248-254`, `sqlite-record-store.ts:375-388`), and the UnknownCallReview schema's `validate` is exactly `decodeUnknownCallReview` over the same `{refKey, schemaId, revision, json}` (`unknown-call-review-codecs.ts:649-658`); the registry enforces one schema per aggregate type (`record-codec.ts:153-173`), and `applyRecordSchema` rejects a changed record and returns the identical encoded record (`record-codec.ts:379-396`). Re-decoding the same pure function on the same bytes therefore cannot fail. A hand-edited or corrupted store is refused earlier, at `owner-record-read.ts:34`, as a store failure (`unavailable`), so tampering does not reach this arm either — that is D2 (the codec/upstream check guarantees the state), not U.

If a fail-closed arm is preferred, collapse it to one fixed `invalid` fallback at `owner-record-read.ts:38` and leave it untested; no tampering test (AGENTS.md rule 4).
